errors.recovery: Set Content-Type to application/json and send a JSON object.

errors.message: The request is malformed or contains unsupported values.
errors.recovery: Check the endpoint schema, required fields, allowed values, size limits and duplicate parameters. Local browser errors can also mean an expired or invalid workflow; begin a new login instead of resubmitting old state.

errors.message: Authentication is required or the credential is invalid.
errors.recovery: Supply a valid credential for this endpoint and issuer. Inspect WWW-Authenticate where present; do not substitute an ID token or print the credential while debugging.
Ask an authorized administrator to review tenant, actor and operation permissions. Do not probe other object identifiers or retry the same operation unchanged.

errors.message: The operation conflicts with the current state.
errors.recovery: Reconcile current state through an authorized read if available. Submit a newly evaluated operation; do not blindly replay a mutation.
Check the configured endpoint and reference using an authorized account. This response is not proof that an object exists or does not exist for another actor.
For readiness probes, retry with bounded backoff. Operators should check validated configuration, migrations and required infrastructure using the foundation runbook.

Read-only operations may use bounded backoff. Before retrying a mutation or credential operation, determine whether it committed; restart authentication when a one-use outcome cannot be reconciled safely.

errors.message: The request could not be completed.
errors.recovery: Keep the request ID and operation time for the operator. Do not blindly retry mutations or one-use credentials; reconcile their outcome first.

errors.message: The request budget is exhausted. Try again after the indicated delay.
errors.recovery: Honor Retry-After. Start a fresh workflow if the original authorization expired. An earlier ambiguous credential request must still be reconciled before retry.
